conventions.convention: The ambient geometry is a smooth boundaryless Lorentzian four-manifold of signature (−,+,+,+), with a separately supplied time orientation; indices run from 0 through 3.

Spacetime orientation is independent of time orientation. The metric volume form is sqrt(|det g|) dx⁰∧dx¹∧dx²∧dx³ in oriented charts. Interior contraction inserts the current into its first slot; charges integrate this three-form over finite smooth singular chains.

The adapted unit normal ν makes (ν,v₁,v₂,v₃) positively oriented. With ε=g(ν,ν), the face coefficient is ε g(J,ν) sqrt(|det(g(vᵢ,vⱼ))|). Null or rank-deficient faces retain their three-form flux but receive no unit-normal formula.

Hilbert variation holds at fixed matter configuration for every jointly smooth metric family equal to the base metric outside one fixed compact set: δS=−(1/(2c))∫T_ab δg^{ab} vol_g. The action domain must admit every compact metric direction.
Dust has strictly positive density coefficient ρ and a future unit timelike field u. In SI, ρ is rest energy density, rest-mass density is ρ/c², and physical four-velocity is cu.
Perfect-fluid density ε and pressure p need not be positive; no equation of state is built into the basic model. The conservation equations remain stated without division by ε+p.

The Einstein-Hilbert normalization is c³/(16πG_N), κ=8πG_N/c⁴, and Λ is constant in the adopted law. The supplied action presentation is scalar-field only; prescribed dust and perfect fluid use the direct equation. A model adopts exactly one presentation.
WEC and SEC test every timelike vector; NEC tests nonzero null vectors; DEC permits the zero energy-current vector in the closed future cone.

load_bearing.statement: For a smooth current on the stated oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, d(ι_J vol_g)=(∇_aJ^a)vol_g and Φ_J(∂C)=∫_C(∇_aJ^a)vol_g for every finite smooth singular four-chain C. If ∂C=Σ₂−Σ₁+B and the divergence vanishes on C, then Φ_J(Σ₂)−Φ_J(Σ₁)=−Φ_J(B).

For the stated jointly smooth Lorentzian metric family equal to g outside compact K contained in one chart, δg^{ab}=−g^{ac}g^{bd}h_cd and the compact chart action difference has derivative ∫_U(G_ab+Λg_ab)q^{ab}w d⁴x. Its timelike-length clause retains the single-chart, C², fixed-endpoint, future-timelike and proper-time hypotheses of the cited curve-variation lemma.

Under the adopted action formulation and the stated Hilbert-tensor hypothesis on M, stationarity of the total action difference under every smooth compactly supported metric variation is equivalent to G_ab+Λg_ab=κT_ab at every point of M.

For the adopted field equation with constant Λ and κ=8πG_N/c⁴ on the open matter domain U, ∇^aT_ab=0 and −S+4Λ=κg^{ab}T_ab. For a perfect fluid, WEC iff ε≥0 and ε+p≥0; NEC iff ε+p≥0; DEC iff ε≥|p|; SEC iff ε+3p≥0 and ε+p≥0.
For a dust model with ρ>0, ∇^aT_ab=0 iff ∇_a(ρu^a)=0 and u^a∇_au^b=0. For the defined perfect-fluid model, ∇^aT_ab=0 iff Dε+(ε+p)ϑ=0 and (ε+p)a^b+h^{ba}∂_ap=0.

The defined scalar tensor represents the metric first variation in the Hilbert convention and obeys ∇^aT_ab=K(□_gφ−V′(φ))∂_bφ. The scalar equation implies conservation; conservation implies the scalar equation where dφ≠0, and everywhere if that set is dense.

Killing fields satisfy ∇_aξ_b+∇_bξ_a=0; g(ξ,γ′) is constant along affinely parametrized geodesics. For symmetric divergence-free T, J^a=T^{ab}ξ_b is divergence-free. Hilbert-tensor conservation in clause (d) requires H1–H4 for every compactly supported smooth ξ and the stated Countable Choice premise.

concerns.concern: Statement (a) begins 'let G be a symmetric bilinear form on V of inertia (3,1,0)' and then concludes that G has that inertia when its matrix is diag(−1,1,1,1)+E with |E_ij|<1/8. This numerical assertion assumes its own conclusion. Proof steps 1.1–2.1 establish the intended assertion for an arbitrary symmetric D+E; downstream examples cite that stronger numerical assertion. The statement should distinguish the arbitrary perturbed form from the Lorentzian base form.

The physical_scope includes a matter tensor represented by its action 'or prescribed and admissible'. The Statement requires a Hilbert tensor, and post-gr-classical-gravitational-action (iii) explicitly says prescribed dust and perfect-fluid sectors do not adopt the variational postulate and have no supplied action. This residual scope wording suggests an additional action branch unsupported by the actual hypotheses.

The Reall sources.references title writes 'delta R = -R_{ab} delta g^{ab} + nabla_a X^a'. With inverse-metric variation q^{ab}, the Ricci contraction has the positive sign, as the item's own step 3.1 correctly computes. A negative contraction corresponds to covariant metric variation after raising its variation indices. The citation annotation needs its sign/index convention checked against the primary passage; this finding concerns the local annotation, not a claimed error in Reall.

alerts.finding: Proof 1.1 says 'The direct presentation and the prescribed-tensor action sectors adopt the same equation on U.' Current post-gr-classical-gravitational-action (iii) says sectors (2) and (3) 'do not adopt this variational postulate' and that no matter action is supplied. The current supplier supports prescribed-tensor direct-equation sectors, not prescribed-tensor action sectors. Factual parentheticals elsewhere in this consumer retain similar wording.

The global-energy paragraph says rem-gr-einstein-matter-scope-and-conventions 'already excludes arbitrary rough or noncompact domains from its smooth branch'. That supplier excludes nonsmooth fields, distributional sources and boundary/junction settings; it does not exclude noncompact smooth manifolds or open domains. The batch expressly defines compact action differences on noncompact M and finite chains within such M. Lack of an exhaustion theorem does not exclude the ambient noncompact domain.

The 'Smooth and finite branch' paragraph lists 'noncompact or rough regions' as outside the branch 'in the sense of rem-gr-einstein-matter-scope-and-conventions'. The cited supplier does not exclude noncompact smooth ambient domains. Its finite-chain restriction limits the integration objects, not the topology or compactness of the ambient matter domain.

L4 states the Killing characterization for a two-dimensional base metric and cites def-gr-killing-field and thm-gr-killing-and-on-shell-matter-identities (a). Those suppliers explicitly concern Lorentzian four-manifolds. Step 4.2 proves the base's symmetrized derivative vanishes, but the equivalence with the Lie-derivative definition in dimension two needs the short dimension-independent coordinate calculation rather than a literal application of the four-dimensional statement.

seams_checked.note: Curvature sign, Ricci contraction and contracted Bianchi divergence are preserved; no claim that the full covariant derivative of G vanishes.
The determinant derivative is applied to invertible smooth coordinate matrix curves on sufficiently small open parameter intervals.
Smooth Lorentzian geometry, inverse metric, causal conventions, SI normalization and adopted-versus-derived status agree.
Tensor differentiation, normal charts and length variation retain the connection and single-chart C² fixed-endpoint proper-time hypotheses.
Tensor slots, raising/lowering and the positive three-dimensional observer rest space are used with their stated meanings.
Flat metric, future direction, null-versus-zero distinction and energy-condition definitions agree.
Constant flat components yield the stated zero Christoffel symbols and coordinate divergence.
Current and finite-chain balance uses are faithful, including side flux and domain restriction. The action-sector and noncompact-domain prose mismatches are recorded in alerts.
Dust uses positive energy-density coefficients and unit velocities; Killing charge signs and side-flux conditions agree. Flat nonzero dust is not claimed to solve Einstein's equation.

Field-law, Killing and dust uses are faithful, with explicit zero-density extension and mass conversion. The numerical perturbation citation uses the intended stronger assertion proved in steps 1.1–2.1, rather than the tautological first assertion as presently worded.
The diagonal-perturbation example L5 cites the arbitrary symmetric 1/8 stability assertion; the supplier proof establishes it, but supplier Statement (a) already assumes Lorentzian inertia.

Four-dimensional Killing contractions and vacuum field-law uses agree. The warped-base lemma applies the four-dimensional Killing characterization to a two-dimensional metric; the short missing generalization is recorded in alerts.
Comoving velocity is unit normalized, ε and p are energy densities, and continuity follows from the full conservation equation without dividing by H.

Exact-solution linearization and alternative action presentation preserve field-law assumptions. Numerical 1/8 perturbation uses share the supplier Statement (a) wording issue; the proof supplies the intended bound.
Field-law references concern constraint necessity and retain the distinction from development existence and uniqueness.
The finite-volume-density lemma uses the chart coefficient sqrt(|det g|) and independently derives its absolute-Jacobian law; it does not assume an oriented volume form on a nonorientable manifold.

Scalar stress and forward conservation, fluid equations and strict EOS restrictions agree. Nonnegative dust is explicitly an extension with independently prescribed geodesic velocity at zeros, not an application of the positive-density converse there.
Radiation EOS and fixed-background linearization use the defined fluid equations; the negative-sound-speed example separates linearized failure from a nonlinear Einstein-fluid claim.

Fixed scalar/fluid models and energy-coefficient dust match the suppliers. Zero-density geodesic velocity is separately required, and maximal-development conclusions retain actual local/restart and choice hypotheses.
